what_happened: The job was meant to move stages S1-S3 of produce_and_verify into run/producer.rs as methods. It was rejected at the final verdict because one check, the test run, failed. The stored output shows only the tail of the test log, and every line shown passes. The failing test is not visible. No acceptance criteria are listed as unmet and no blocker or major findings are listed. So the stored fields do not show whether the move broke something, or whether the failure was already there.
cause: Nothing runs the repo's test suite on the base commit before the job, so the verdict cannot tell a failure the job caused from one that was already there. The failure record also keeps only the tail of the log, which shows passing tests, so the failing test is not named in the stored event. A failed check ends the verdict as fail without anyone judging the criteria. Whether the cause is the move or a pre-existing failure is an inference, since the stored fields do not show it.
prevention: Run the same test command on the base commit when a job is admitted and record which tests fail. When a check fails after the job, compare the two runs and say whether each failing test is new or already failing. Store the names and output of the failing tests, not only the log tail. Still judge every acceptance criterion even when a check fails, so a failed check does not leave all criteria unjudged. This would cover the whole class of rejections caused by a failing check with no baseline.
proposed_request: Retry the job that moves produce_and_verify stages S1-S3 into run/producer.rs as methods. Outcome: the move is done, the repo's full test suite passes, and behavior is unchanged. First run the full test suite on the unchanged base and record which tests, if any, already fail. After the move, run it again and name any failing test, with its output, and say whether it was failing before the move. If the move caused a failure, fix it inside the move's scope. If a test was already failing before the move, report it and do not widen the job to fix it.
